name: Jesse Gabriel
title: California State Assemblymember, Chair of the Assembly Budget Committee
background: Gabriel earned a B.A. in political science from the University of California, Berkeley in 2004 and a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 2008. Before entering the Legislature he practiced as a constitutional rights attorney in state and federal courts, work that according to his official Assembly biography included representing DACA recipients ('Dreamers'), Holocaust survivors, domestic violence victims, and communities facing discrimination. He also worked as an attorney with the United States Senate and served as a Los Angeles County commissioner.

Gabriel was first elected to the Assembly in a 2018 special election, defeating Justin Clark 65.7%–34.3% to represent the 45th Assembly District. He was re-elected in 2020 (66.2% against Jeffi Girgenti) and 2022, when post-redistricting he ran and won in the renumbered 46th Assembly District against Dana Caruso (65.4%). He was re-elected again in 2024 against Tracey Schroeder (62.9%) and advanced in the June 2026 primary with 62.1% of the vote.

In the Legislature, Gabriel chairs the Assembly Budget Committee and, per his official Assembly biography, has authored more than fifty bills signed into law, including several described as first-in-the-nation measures such as the California Food Safety Act and a state Victims of Crime Act. He resides in the San Fernando Valley with his wife, affordable-housing attorney Rachel Rosner, and their three sons.
voting_record_highlights: ACA 20 (2025–2026), the 'Save for California's Future Act' that became Proposition 2 on the November 2026 ballot: Gabriel was lead Assembly author. It passed the Assembly 59–8 and the Senate 29–2 on June 25, 2026, clearing the two-thirds constitutional-amendment threshold, and Gabriel signed the official ballot argument in favor as Assembly Budget Committee chair. (Source: Ballotpedia, ACA 20/Proposition 2 page.)

AB 418 (2023–2024), the California Food Safety Act, which Gabriel authored: it prohibits the manufacture, sale, or distribution in California of food products containing brominated vegetable oil, potassium bromate, propylparaben, or red dye 3, with civil penalties up to $10,000 for repeat violations. The Assembly concurred in Senate amendments 65–6 on September 12, 2023; the Governor signed it October 7, 2023 (effective January 1, 2027). (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill text and status for AB 418.)

AB 28 (2023–2024), the Gun Violence Prevention and School Safety Act, co-authored by Gabriel with Assemblymember Kevin McCarty (Sen. Anthony Portantino as principal coauthor): it imposes an 11% excise tax on retail sales of firearms, ammunition, and firearm precursor parts (effective July 1, 2024), funding violence-intervention and school-safety programs, with exemptions for law enforcement and small dealers. The Senate concurred in Assembly amendments 57–17 on September 7, 2023; the Governor signed it September 26, 2023 as Chapter 231, Statutes of 2023. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill text and status for AB 28.)
attendance: No individual floor-attendance or voting-participation record for Gabriel specifically was found. Unlike some city councils that publish member-by-member meeting attendance, the California State Assembly does not appear to publish a comparable individual attendance record; the California Legislature's leginfo.legislature.ca.gov system publishes bill-by-bill roll-call votes (which show whether a member voted aye, no, or did not vote on a given measure) rather than a cumulative attendance score, and no such cumulative record for Gabriel was located on his official Assembly site or on Ballotpedia.
